content: Medically indigent adults (MIAs) in the United States healthcare system are individuals who lack health insurance and are not eligible for other forms of healthcare coverage, such as Medicaid, Medicare, or private health insurance. State, county, or municipal government programs designed for MIAs may assist these individuals in accessing medical care by covering all or part of the costs associated with their healthcare. These programs are generally considered a last resort and are only available to individuals who meet specific socioeconomic eligibility criteria that define them as being in a last resort situation.
